If I'm correct TW's are used to warn sensitive people about content they might find unsettling, but why did this become a thing in feminist circles and why is it so very exaggerated?
Why and how did "Trigger Warnings" become popular?

It's an accountability thing. For years, people were fine taking responsibility and shielding themselves from content that would offend them. Now it's everyone else's responsibility to make you feel "safe" on the internet, because God forbid you take responsibility for your own idiosyncrasies.

When I first came across trigger warnings, they were for content that could legitimately trigger a post-traumatic episode. I think it was a detailed first-person account of a child's sexual abuse at the hands of a family member. People who'd been through a similar experience and "moved on" could have disturbing flashbacks they'd rather avoid.

What's important to note is that the person posting the story included the warning as a courtesy. There was not an expectation that he do it. No one would react in outrage if he didn't. And the trigger he warned about was genuine psychological anguish, not "being offended." It's evolved from a useful form of politeness into a display of entitlement and outrage.

It's a thing that some people did when they are worried about a post, etc triggering PTSD or similar in people who have been through similar experiences. Like you might warn your uncle who gets 'Nam flashbacks before watching this war movie with you.

Unfortunately, it has devolved from something you do when you are trying to be nice to a group to something that certain groups expect you to do for every sensitive group ever. And then they went and expanded from sensitive groups to anything that could offend. And then they managed to find an offended someone for each thing out there. And then the rest of us thought the whole thing was ridiculous so, to make fun of them, you see warnings or requests for warnings on things that didn't even exist before.

I don't think it's a feminist thing so much as the people who earnestly believe in triggers everywhere are often feminist. The two attitudes are correlated, but (just guessing here) it's probably that the attitudes that make people want triggers also pushes them toward feminism.

I have to admit I don't know enough about PTSD to make any kind of educated statement, but I've always been under the impression that sharing your difficult experiences and reliving said experiences is often therapeutic and can ease your suffering in the long run. At least that's what cognitive behavioral therapy is based on. Seeing all these TW's might cause more anxiety as you limit and shield yourself from issues you should be confronting, dealing with?

Is there any kind of science backing this that started the whole trend of TW or is it just regular people trying to be considerate gone too far?

Well, it's not just PTSD. There are other mental health issues that are exacerbated by "triggers" (and that is a word commonly used by mental health professionals). e.g. Relapse into addiction can be triggered by hanging out with certain people, being in a certain place, a particular smell, or even just being told "this beer is so tasty, you just HAVE to try it".

CBT (cognitive behavioral therapy) is based on teaching the sufferer to understand their issues, how they grow, and recognizing what gives them trouble, then learning to figure out how to stop themselves from having the issues. In effect, they learn to shield themselves so they can have a semblance of a normal life. But they could still get blindsided and have an issue too severe or too quick to stop.

There are other types of therapy that do what you are saying. Different people and different issues in the same person need different treatment. Many therapies teach you to identify and avoid triggers.

There's no science behind it being everywhere. That's like trying to pad the entire world and ban all knives because one person out there is such a klutz. You could pad their home and office though. Similarly, it makes sense to add trigger warnings for rape victims on a rape victim support board.

Then some people make fun of the "pad the world" types because they don't think there's a point in trying to pad a tomato. So they say things like "you forgot to pad the koosh ball".
It's sort of like the "56k warning" from ye olden days of the internet, except for PTSD.

Rice is a staple and while you can cook it fairly easily on a stove top. A rice cooker can be had for under $20 and is the most fool proof method of cooking rice perfectly every time.

Plain white rice is the most common and cheapest. Although you can try other types like Brown or Jasmine. There are more varieties of rice than colors of the rainbow.

Make sure to read the instructions that come with your cooker but as a general rule the water to rice ratio is always 2 to 1. That means 2 cups of water for every one cup of rice.

You also always want to make sure to rinse your rice before you cook it, the easiest way is to put the desired amount in a large bowl and run it under the tap while stirring with your hand until the water is clear.

The actual process will depend on the cooker, but in most cases you just combine your water and rice in the cooker, put the lid on and start the process.

However you don't strictly have to just use rice and water. You can kick it up a notch by giving it a shot with your spice weasel before you start the process (I keed I keed!!) But you can add spices and falvorings like chicken base, fresh garlic, or even cilantro and lime which is one of my favorite combos.
